scope_description.value: Complete design for replacement of three geared traction elevators in Building 510 at Norfolk Naval Shipyard: freight elevator #64 (20,000 lb, Class C2, 5 stops, WO 1741405) and freight elevator #63 (20,000 lb, Class C2, 7 stops) plus passenger elevator #67 (2,500 lb, Class A, 6 stops) (WO 1741675). Scope includes new cabs, machines, controllers, hoistway doors, fire protection modifications, ductless split HVAC for machine rooms, sump pumps, electrical service modifications, hazardous materials abatement (ACM, LBP, PCBs), structural reinforcement of machine beams, and all code upgrades per UFC 3-490-06 and ASME A17.1–2019.

sheets.title: General Data / Hoistway Plan / Pit Plan — Elevator #63
sheets.reading_notes: Shows Class C2 freight elevator #63 data block: 20,000 lb capacity, 100 FPM, 75 HP motor, 2:1 roping, 9 hoist cables at 3/4". Machine Hollister-Whitney #74. Hoistway plan shows 21'-1" clear hoistway width, 11'-8" clear depth. Pit plan shows 6'3" pit depth. Car guide rail loads tabulated with static/dynamic values (R1–R5). Buffer loads shown. Seismic Design Category A (provisions not required).

sheets.title: Machine Room Plan — Elevators #63 & #67
sheets.reading_notes: Combined machine room plan for #63 and #67 (shared room). Machine room approximately 24'-0" x 24'-10" as noted in VT report text. Shows HW #74 overhead traction machine, MCE controller, overspeed governor new location, dead-end assemblies, fused disconnect locations. Custom base modification to avoid machine room wall noted. Estimated heat gain Elev #63: 20,265 BTU/hr.

sheets.title: Sling & Platform / Section A-A / Section B-B — Elevator #63
sheets.reading_notes: Shows car sling structure (W10x45 stiles, MC13x31.8 crosshead and safety plank), platform (3/8" steel raised pattern floor plate), 68' travel (Elev #64 per comparison). Counterweight runby 2'-0" initial / 1'-6" final. Guide rail schedule: car rails 30 lb, CWT rails 15 lb. Floor elevation table: floors 1–7 + roof, 17'-0" floor-to-floor (floors 2–7). Pit FL at 96'-8-3/4" elevation.

sheets.title: General Data / Machine Room Plan / Elevator #64
sheets.reading_notes: Data block for Elev #64: Class C2, 20,000 lb, 100 FPM, 75 HP, 2:1 roping. Machine room plan (different from #63/#67 machine room): approximately 17'-6" x 22'-9" per VT text. Shows HW #74 machine location, MCE controller, overspeed governor, dead-end assemblies. Estimated heat gain Elev #64: 20,265 BTU/hr. 68'-0" total travel. 9'-0.5" clear hoistway (N/S direction) x 13'-8" (E/W direction).

sheets.title: Sling & Platform / Sections / Head & Sill — Elevator #64
sheets.reading_notes: Car sling detail (W10x45 stiles, MC13x31.8 crosshead), 3/8" floor plate, 10'-0" cab height. 72'-2" clear overhead in hoistway. 6'-3.5" pit depth. Total travel 68'-0". Floor schedule: 6 floors, 17'-0" floor-to-floor (floors 2–6), 6'-3.25" pit clearance. Pit floor at 96'-7-3/4". Head and sill detail shows power bi-parting door: 10'-2-3/4" clear opening, truckable sill.

sheets.title: Counterweight Rail Bracket / Pit Rail Bracket Detail — Elevator #64
sheets.reading_notes: Rail bracket details for new installation. New car rails welded to horizontal I-beams with 3/4" post-installed anchor. Bracket spacing not to exceed 3'-0" between rail clips. Horizontal beam spacing varies from 2'-10" to 4'-0" (existing). Shows counterweight rail bracket elevations and new car rail attachment method. Note: Maximum bracket spacing 3'-0"; tie brackets required for spans >12'-2".

sheets.title: Passenger Elevator #67 Layout Sheets (1 of 6 through 6 of 6)
sheets.reading_notes: Complete 6-sheet layout package for Elev #67 by Hollister-Whitney (Layout L-9143-1). Sheet 1: General data (2,500 lb, 350 FPM, Class A, 6 landings), car construction (C8x11.5 crosshead, C7x9.8 stiles), estimated weights (total car 5,400 lb, total CWT 6,400 lb), overhead reactions (R1=12,507#, R2=7,971#, R3=9,545#, R4=5,450#). Sheet 2: Pit plan (6'-3" pit depth). Sheet 3: Hoistway plan (6'-10" B-B rails, 3'-2" D.B.G., 6'-3" D.B.G.). Sheet 4: Machine room overall plan (shares room with #63, machine room 24'-0"x24'-10"). Sheet 5: Machine room detail — HW #54 OH machine, 25 HP motor, MCE Motion 4000 controller, rope gripper HW #622. Sheet 6: Hoistway section (84'-5" travel, 6'-3" pit, 12'-2" clear headroom). Note: Preliminary drawings, labeled 'NOT FOR FABRICATION OR CONSTRUCTION', dated 05-22-2023.

sheets.title: 3D Laser Scan Elevation Sections — Elevator #63 and #64
sheets.reading_notes: 3D point cloud and model elevation sections for Elevs #63 and #64 by WadeLynn Geospatial LLC, dated 6/23/2023 (#63) and 6/29/2023 (#64). Color-coded deviation maps show as-built vs. plumb line. Overall max deviation: 0'-1-11/32" at corners (#63); 0'-1-29/32" at corners (#64). Elevation sections show floor-to-floor heights confirming 17'-0" typical and pit depths. Reading notes: #64 hoistway shows larger plumb deviation (nearly 2 inches at corners) which may have influenced structural analysis and new bracket sizing.

hvac: Ductless split air conditioning system (outdoor unit + wall-mounted fan coil) for each elevator machine room (Elevs #63/#67 machine room: one unit; Elev #64 machine room: one unit). Design conditions: 72°F / 50% RH cooling, 50°F heating. Estimated heat gain: 20,265 BTU/hr per machine room.
Existing steam radiators to be demolished; steam and condensate piping removed to point outside machine rooms.
DDC controls required per SAES, connecting to NNSY base-wide DDC system.
electrical: Elev #64: 460V/3-phase/60Hz, 75HP motor, 106A full load. Fed from Substation 510-B (1000/1120 KVA, 11.5kV-480Y/277V transformer, 1600A switchboard), bucket 510-B-3 (Westinghouse 800A DS-206, 400A rated).

Elevs #63/#67: 460V/3-phase/60Hz. Elev #63: 75HP motor, 106A. Elev #67: 25HP motor. Fed from Substation 510-A (1500 KVA, 11.5kV-480Y/277V, 1600A switchboard), bucket #3 (Westinghouse 800A DS-206, 400A).
LED lighting (4000K, min 80 CRI): machine room min 19 fc, elevator shaft min 10 fc.
Cat-6 copper telephone cables for emergency elevator phone service.
Two-way emergency communications: master intercom in each machine room + lobby station at first floor.
Security (Elev #63): roll-up door with keypad access controller and fire-rated sight glass at first floor interior landing.
plumbing: Submersible sump pump for each elevator pit (discharge to building exterior via schedule 40 PVC). Automatic, electric motor-driven.
Required discharge: 50 GPM per elevator per UFC 3-490-06.
fire_protection: Fire alarm modifications to coordinate with Mircom FX-MNS system being installed by concurrent Project P-256. Heat detectors at exterior landings (1st floor Elev #64; 1st and 7th floor Elev #63). Control modules relocated within 3' of elevator controller for FEO relay.

Dedicated sprinkler line from 6th floor to each machine room, with supervised shut-off valve, check valve, waterflow switch (no time delay), and test valve located outside machine room. Sprinklers in machine rooms with guards.
Waterflow switch directly connected to elevator shunt trip breaker (instantaneous).

conflict_flags.rationale: VT consultant (James Lawrence & Associates) physically inspected the equipment, reviewed data tags, and dated original installation to 1955. SAES references building construction records and likely conflates building construction year (1956) with elevator installation year. VT inspection-based finding is more authoritative for elevator age.

Detailed construction schedule in the Final Design BOD (December 2023) supersedes the SAES estimate (September 2022). The BOD schedule was developed after design completion and reflects more accurate scheduling.

R1 is the later document (Revision 1, dated 09/26/22). The '/X003' modifier in the original SAES may represent a draft task order identifier that was dropped in the final revision. The base IDIQ contract number N40085-20-D0005 is consistent across all documents.

SAES ECC of $2.5M is the government-approved program amount for all construction trades combined. VT consultant range of $2M–$4M is for elevator contractor work only, which is typically 60–80% of total ECC for this type of project. Values are not directly comparable. SAES value used as design contract value.
